title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: vignette focuses association term construction, including transformation selection, interpretability, practical trade-offs. also explains association terms propagate public summary, draw-extraction, plotting APIs labels used consistently tables, MCMC plots, fitted association curves. Association transforms apply supported longitudinal families (including double_exponential, skew_double_exponential, beta, cumulative_logit) competing-risk survival models. event time default 15 Gauss-Kronrod nodes used integration (configurable), longitudinal linear predictor decomposed mean component marker component. components, JoiNMe constructs: CV_total: total current value (mean + marker components). CV_mean: current value mean component . CV_marker: current value marker component . CS_total: total current slope, approximated forward finite difference rescaled original time units. CS_mean: slope mean component. CS_marker: slope marker component. CORR: subject-specific variance summary marker--id covariance structure, constant across time. VCOV: subject-specific lower-triangular summary marker--id Cholesky factor L, also constant across time. channel uses entries L directly rather reconstructed covariance matrix L L'. component can included excluded using assoc argument. assoc include component, corresponding coefficient prior-enter likelihood. JoiNMe reports association survival-process coefficients linear predictor scale first. internal time normalisation used Stan model recovered linear scale exponentiation. multiplicative interpretations: summary(fit)$tables$baseline_hazard reports baseline-hazard coefficients log scale hazard-ratio scale. intercept adjusted -log(tmax); non-intercept basis coefficients unchanged. summary(fit)$tables$survival_process reports baseline covariate coefficients Hazard.Ratio interval columns exponentiated log-scale summaries. summary(fit)$tables$assoc reports association coefficients native linear scale (including marker-weight terms active). intercept-baseline adjustment follows proportional-hazards identity internal time scaling contributes constant offset log-hazard scale. Therefore intercept shifted; spline/formula basis terms kept fitted. CORR VCOV components require marker--id random effects. marker block include inner ( ... | id ) term, Q_idm = 0 covariance-style associations available.

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: multiple biomarkers modelled, JoiNMe constructs marker-average association components using weights \omega_d (one per marker). marker-aggregated terms (cv_total, cv_marker, cs_total, cs_marker), transforms applied marker level first averaged weights. matters whenever transforms nonlinear. example, marker-specific total current values CV_{id}(t) transform f_{cv}: ext{cv\_total}(t) = \frac{1}{D}\sum_{d=1}^{D} \omega_d\, f_{cv}\!\left(CV_{id}(t)\right), differs f_{cv}(\frac{1}{D}\sum_d \omega_d CV_{id}(t)) unless f_{cv} linear. slopes, let CS_{id}(t) marker-specific slope feature f_{cs} configured CS transform. ext{cs\_total}(t) = \frac{1}{D}\sum_{d=1}^{D} \omega_d\, f_{cs}\!\left(CS_{id}(t)\right), analogously cs_marker. intentionally equal f_{cs}(\frac{1}{D}\sum_d \omega_d CS_{id}(t)) unless f_{cs} linear. practice, provide fixed weights marker_weights fixed_marker_weights = TRUE, set fixed_marker_weights = FALSE use signed perturbations around base weights, \omega_d = \omega_d^{(0)} + z_d. shrinkage switch controls standardized latent family fitting simulation: 0 Student-t_6(0,1), 1 Laplace(0,1), 2 Normal(0,1). estimated weights supplied base, \omega^{(0)}=0. simulator stores base, latent, effective truths truth$marker_weights_base, truth$marker_weights_latent, truth$marker_weights; last effective weight used generate survival times. Use posterior_assoc(fit, summary = TRUE) (assoc(fit, summary = TRUE)) extract association-specific posterior summaries without requiring full model summary. Use summary = FALSE obtain posterior draws per association term. Association terms can extracted directly reporting scale draws(). canonical posterior variables alpha_cv_total, alpha_cs_total, alpha_cv_mean, alpha_cs_mean, alpha_corr[...], alpha_vcov[...]. coefficient actually used event hazard, also scale reported summary() used prediction plotting methods. Conditional effects distinct subject-specific dynamic prediction. conditional_effects() varies named predictors holding predictors explicit profile values can return longitudinal process, event process, . longitudinal estimand population-level expected marker response default. Set longitudinal_estimand = "marker" retain fitted marker-level deviation, "marginal_marker" average marker-specific predictions within posterior draw. marker averaging occurs inverse-link transformation, targets average expected response rather expected response average marker effect. event estimand direct relative-hazard component exp(W * gamma); baseline hazard longitudinal association contribution held fixed making event-covariate comparisons.

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: joinme supports following transformation families association features: Identity (type = "identity"): transformation. Functional (type = "functional"): user-defined expression converted fixed bytecode program. Monotone -spline (type = "ispline" "ispline_penalised"): smooth monotone mapping. Bounded-domain monotone -spline (type = "ispline_expit" "ispline_expit_penalised"): monotone spline machinery, applied plogis(x) rather directly x. Ordered piecewise linear (type = "pwlin"): posterior interpolation across fixed knots monotone knot ordinates estimated Stan. Interpretation note recovery experiments: use fixed spline (type = "ispline" expit variant explicit coeff), association coefficient interpretable fixed transformed scale can checked directly simulate-fit recovery tests. use jointly estimated penalised spline (*_penalised), transform shape association coefficient learned together. fitted alpha still meaningful inside model, coefficient recovery typically weaker fixed-transform case data must learn transformed scale hazard weight simultaneously. Syntax: list(type = "identity") Default transform term omitted set NULL. parameters used. Syntax: list(type = "functional", expr = ~ log1p(x)) Required field: expr. defaults beyond supplied expression. Syntax: list(type = "ispline", knots = c(-1, 0, 1), coeff = c(0, 0.3, 0.8, 1.1, 1.3)) Required fields: knots, coeff. Default: degree = 3 omitted. Syntax: list(type = "ispline_penalised", x = seq(-2, 2, length.= 50), n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1) Defaults: n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1. knots omitted Stan-estimated mode, derived x quantiles. Syntax: list(type = "ispline_expit_penalised", x = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.= 50), n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1) Defaults: n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1. raw association feature mapped plogis(x) runtime, spline basis built bounded domain. Supply training x explicit knots directly expit scale [0, 1] fitted spline domain matches runtime basis. Syntax: list(type = "pwlin", knots = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), direction = "increasing"). Required field: knots (aliases: cutpoints legacy x). Default: direction = "increasing"; use "decreasing" falling transform. optional non-negative lambda penalises second differences ordered knot ordinates; defaults zero.

Modelling mode: omit y, keep knots (n_knots) plus lambda, Stan estimates monotone spline coefficients jointly rest model. Meaning arguments: x: raw association-feature values, used either training inputs help choose knots. y: optional target transformed values x points. present, telling package shape want approximate. lambda: smoothness penalty weight (higher = smoother, lower = flexible). code: sim <- simulate_joinme(   n_id = 100,   families = rep("student_t", 5),   n_obs_per_marker_per_id = 10,   times_obs = seq(0, 8, length.out = 14),   quadrature_nodes = 31,   seed = 123,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   assoc_coefs = c(cv_total = 0.6) )  # Gauss-Kronrod nodes/weights are fixed in Stan; `quadrature_nodes` selects # the node count used to build the design matrices in R.  # Formula links are inverted symbolically; custom inverse-links can be supplied # directly via jm_family(..., inv_link = ~ ...).  # When estimating marker weights, compare against sim$truth$marker_weights # because weights are used directly in Stan. formulaLong <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time || id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time || id) || marker)  formulaEvent <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2  fit <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong,   dataLong = sim$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent,   dataEvent = sim$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = rep('student_t',5),   transforms = joinme_tf(cv_total = "identity"),   priors = joinme_priors(),   control = list(     parallel_chains = 2,     iter_warmup = 300,     iter_sampling = 700,     seed = 123,     refresh = 100,     adapt_delta = 0.75,     max_treedepth=12,     init = 1     # engine = 'rstan'   ) ) fit2 <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong,   dataLong = sim$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent,   dataEvent = sim$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   transforms = joinme_tf(cv_total = "identity"),   priors = joinme_priors(beta = list(scale = 1.5), alpha = list(scale = 1.5), lkj = 2),   basehaz = "bs",   n_knots = 5,   basehaz_degree = 3,   control = list(iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500, adapt_delta = 0.9) ) sum_obj <- summary(fit) print(sum_obj)  # Sampler diagnostics diag_tbl <- as.data.frame(t(unlist(sum_obj$diagnostics))) knitr::kable(diag_tbl, digits = 3, caption = "Sampler diagnostics (scenario A).")  # Fixed effects (beta) fixef_tbl <- sum_obj$tables$fixef truth_beta <- sim$truth$beta_long  fixef_tbl$truth <- truth_beta[fixef_tbl$term] fixef_tbl$bias <- fixef_tbl$Estimate - fixef_tbl$truth fixef_tbl$covered <- fixef_tbl$truth >= fixef_tbl$Q2.5 &   fixef_tbl$truth <= fixef_tbl$Q97.5  fixef_view <- fixef_tbl[, c("term", "Estimate", "Q2.5", "Q97.5", "truth", "bias", "covered")] knitr::kable(fixef_view, digits = 3, caption = "Fixed effects summary (scenario A).")  # Survival covariates (gamma_w) if (!is.null(sum_obj$tables$gamma_w)) {   gamma_tbl <- sum_obj$tables$gamma_w   truth_gamma <- sim$truth$beta_event    gamma_tbl$truth <- truth_gamma[gamma_tbl$term]   gamma_tbl$bias <- gamma_tbl$Estimate - gamma_tbl$truth   gamma_tbl$covered <- gamma_tbl$truth >= gamma_tbl$Q2.5 &     gamma_tbl$truth <= gamma_tbl$Q97.5    gamma_view <- gamma_tbl[, c("term", "Estimate", "Q2.5", "Q97.5", "truth", "bias", "covered")]   knitr::kable(gamma_view, digits = 3, caption = "Survival covariate summary (scenario A).") }  # Association (aggregate CV total) if (!is.null(sum_obj$tables$assoc)) {   assoc_tbl <- sum_obj$tables$assoc   alpha_total_hat <- assoc_tbl$Estimate[assoc_tbl$term %in% c("cv_total")]   alpha_total_bias <- alpha_total_hat - sim$truth$alpha_cv_total   list(alpha_total_hat = alpha_total_hat, alpha_total_bias = alpha_total_bias) }  # Renamed posterior draws and MCMC visualisation draws(fit, variables = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), format = "draws_df") mcmc_plot(fit, variable = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), type = "trace") pred_fit <- posterior_epred(   fit,   newdataLong = sim$dataLong,   newdataEvent = code: sim_comp <- simulate_joinme(   n_id = 40,   families = rep("student_t", 3),   n_obs_per_marker_per_id = 6,   times_obs = seq(0, 8, length.out = 12),   seed = 444,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   assoc_coefs = c(cv_total = 0.6) )  # Simulate cause-specific event times and derive event_type from the minimum time. set.seed(444) cause_levels <- c("cause1", "cause2") time_cens <- 8.0  h0_list <- list(   cause1 = weibull_h0(shape = 1.2, scale = 5.0),   cause2 = weibull_h0(shape = 2.0, scale = 7.0) )  gamma_w_mat <- rbind(   cause1 = c("(Intercept)" = -0.2, "x1" = 0.4, "x2" = -0.3),   cause2 = c("(Intercept)" = 0.1, "x1" = -0.2, "x2" = 0.5) )  find_bracket <- function(f, lower = 0, upper = 1, upper_max = 50, expand = 1.7, max_expand = 60L) {   f_lower <- f(lower)   if (!is.finite(f_lower) || f_lower > 0) return(NULL)   f_upper <- f(upper)   if (!is.finite(f_upper)) return(NULL)   it <- 0L   while (f_upper < 0 && upper < upper_max && it < max_expand) {     upper <- min(upper_max, upper * expand)     f_upper <- f(upper)     if (!is.finite(f_upper)) return(NULL)     it <- it + 1L   }   if (f_upper >= 0) list(lower = lower, upper = upper) else NULL }  draw_cause_time <- function(i, k) {   haz_row <- c("(Intercept)" = 1, "x1" = sim_comp$dataEvent$x1[i], "x2" = sim_comp$dataEvent$x2[i])   eta_w <- sum(haz_row * gamma_w_mat[k, ])   alpha_cv <- sim_comp$truth$alpha_cv_total   h0 <- h0_list[[k]]    hazard_i <- function(t) h0(t) * exp(eta_w + alpha_cv * sim_comp$helpers$cv_total(i, t))   cumhaz_i <- function(t) {     if (t <= 0) return(0)     out <- integrate(hazard_i, lower = 0, upper = t, rel.tol = 1e-6, subdivisions = 2000L)     as.numeric(out$value)   }    U <- runif(1)   target <- -log(U)   f_root <- function(t) cumhaz_i(t) - target   br <- find_bracket(f_root, lower = 0, upper = 1, upper_max = 50)   if (is.null(br)) return(list(time = time_cens, event = 0L))   T <- uniroot(f_root, lower = br$lower, upper = br$upper)$root   if (T > time_cens) list(time = time_cens, event = 0L) else list(time = T, event = 1L) }  event_time <- numeric(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent)) event_type <- character(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent)) event_flag <- integer(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent))  for (i in seq_len(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent))) {   times_k <- vapply(cause_levels, function(k) draw_cause_time(i, k)$time, numeric(1))   min_idx <- which.min(times_k)   event_time[i] <- times_k[min_idx]   event_flag[i] <- as.integer(event_time[i] < time_cens)   event_type[i] <- cause_levels[min_idx]   if (event_flag[i] == 0L) {     event_type[i] <- cause_levels[1]   } }  sim_comp$dataEvent$time <- event_time sim_comp$dataEvent$event <- event_flag sim_comp$dataEvent$event_type <- factor(event_type, levels = cause_levels)  sim_comp$dataLong <- sim_comp$dataLong |>   dplyr::inner_join(sim_comp$dataEvent[, c("id", "time")], by = "id", suffix = c("", "_event")) |>   dplyr::filter(time <= time_event) |>   dplyr::select(-time_event) formulaLong_comp <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time || id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time || id) || marker)  formulaEvent_comp <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2  fit_comp <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong_comp,   dataLong = sim_comp$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent_comp,   dataEvent = sim_comp$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = rep("student_t", 3),   transforms = joinme_tf(cv_total = "identity"),   event_type_var = "event_type",   control = list(     engine = "cmdstanr",     chains = 1,     parallel_chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 150,     iter_sampling = 150,     seed = 444,     refresh = 0,     adapt_delta = 0.85,     max_treedepth = 10   ) ) id_comp <- 1 ndL_comp <- sim_comp$dataLong[sim_comp$dataLong$id == id_comp, ] ndE_comp <- sim_comp$dataEvent[sim_comp$dataEvent$id == id_comp, ]  time_start_comp <- max(ndL_comp$time) times_comp <- seq(time_start_comp, time_start_comp + 2, length.out = 40)  pred_comp <- predict(   fit_comp,   newdataLong = ndL_comp,   newdataEvent = ndE_comp,   process = "event",   time_start = time_start_comp,   times = times_comp,   control = list(     n_samples = 100,     engine = "cmdstanr",     chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 0,     iter_sampling = 1, code: if (!require('joinme', quietly = TRUE)) {   if (requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE) && file.exists(file.path(repo_root, "DESCRIPTION"))) {     devtools::load_all(repo_root, quiet = TRUE)   } else {     try(base::attachNamespace("joinme"), silent = TRUE)   } } library(survival)  set.seed(2026)

title: Introduction to Joint Nested Mixed Effects Models
text: generate modest dataset workflow runs quickly still containing longitudinal survival information.

what: Step 3: Specify longitudinal and survival models
title: Introduction to Joint Nested Mixed Effects Models
text: longitudinal formula defines fixed effects random effects. survival formula defines baseline covariates hazard model. Formula-scoped weighting can declared directly grouping terms via weighted(group, weights = <column>), including marker-level grouping declarations.
code: formulaLong <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time || id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time || id) || marker)  formulaEvent <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2 formulaLong_weighted <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time | weighted(id, weights = id_w)) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time | weighted(id, weights = id_w)) | weighted(marker, weights = marker_w))

title: Introduction to Joint Nested Mixed Effects Models
text: link survival hazard current value (CV) longitudinal process using identity transformation.
code: fit <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong,   dataLong = sim$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent,   dataEvent = sim$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = "student_t",   transforms = joinme_tf(cv_total = "identity"),   basehaz = joinme_basehaz('bs'),    control = list(     engine = "rstan",     chains = 1,     parallel_chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 500,     iter_sampling = 500,     seed = 2026,     refresh = 0,     adapt_delta = 0.85   ) )

title: Technical Specification and Implementation Details
text: document provides formal technical specification joinme package model structure. details precise matrix formulations, transformation logic, exact algorithms used underlying Stan engine. Ideally, document serves reference advanced methodologists developers seeking understand extend package internals.

title: Technical Specification and Implementation Details
text: joint model consists two linked submodels: multivariate longitudinal mixed-effects model survival model time-varying covariates defined longitudinal process. N: Number subjects (= 1, \dots, N). title: The JoiNMe Framework: Methodology and Statistical Theory
text: joint likelihood product longitudinal likelihood \mathcal{L}_{Long} survival likelihood \mathcal{L}_{Surv}: p(\theta, \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w} | \mathbf{y}, \mathbf{T}, \boldsymbol{\delta}) \propto \left[ \prod_{=1}^N \prod_{d=1}^D \prod_{j=1}^{n_{id}} p(y_{idj} | \mathbf{u}_i, \mathbf{v}_d, \mathbf{w}_{id}) \right] \times \left[ \prod_{=1}^N \lambda_i(T_i)^{\delta_i} \exp\left(-\int_0^{T_i} \lambda_i(s) ds\right) \right] \times p(\text{priors}) JoiNMe compiles model Stan program. Key efficiency features include: Analytic Gradient Log-Likelihood: Stan’s autodiff engine handles complex chain rule derivatives required joint likelihood. Multithreading via reduce_sum: likelihood calculation parallelised subjects (“grainsize”). allows linear scaling number available CPU cores. Gauss-Kronrod Quadrature: survival integral \int_0^{T_i} \lambda_i(s) ds approximated using Gauss-Kronrod rule (default 15-point, configurable) high accuracy modest computational cost. Default priors weakly informative aligned Stan implementation: Fixed effects distributional regressions: regression coefficients longitudinal survival covariates use Student-t priors 6 degrees freedom, centred 0, user-specified default scales. heavier tails stabilise inference keeping weak regularisation. Association coefficients: CV/CS total, mean, marker coefficients use non-centred parameterisation \alpha = z_{\alpha} \cdot sd_{\alpha}. marker-weight-involving channels (cv_total, cs_total, cv_marker, cs_marker), first active latent sign-anchored non-negative improve identifiability; channels remain free positive negative. Marker weights: estimated, marker-weight perturbations use additive latent form around user-supplied base weights. shrinkage = 0, 1, 2 selects standard Student-t_6, Laplace, Normal latents, respectively. resulting signed weights enter marker-aggregated association terms without additional normalisation. simulate_joinme() uses identical switch defaults zero base simulates estimated weights. Random-effect scales: subject, marker, marker--subject standard deviations use half-normal priors original scale weakly informative positivity constraints. Random-effect correlations: correlation matrices use LKJ-Cholesky prior concentration parameter \eta, allowing mild regularisation toward identity remaining flexible. Baseline hazard: baseline level encoded intercept basis column bs_gamma_c (standalone log_h0_intercept parameter). Spline coefficients penalised via second-difference priors excluding intercept-basis column, providing smoothness control baseline hazard. Penalised transformations: type = "ispline_penalised", -spline coefficients use smoothness penalty (second differences) stabilise nonlinear association transforms sparse time regions. Family-specific parameters: scale parameters use exponential priors, Student-t degrees freedom use gamma priors, skewness parameters (0,1) use beta priors, matching parameter support.

Focus on survival and cumhaz     control = list(progress = FALSE) # just to silence the progress bar   ),   error = function(e) {     message("Prediction skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))     NULL   } )  head(preds$predictions$survival) #>     id     time  Survival    Median  Est.Error       L95       U95 #> 7.1  7 4.000000 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.00000000 1.0000000 1.0000000 #> 7.2  7 4.137931 0.9813482 0.9848616 0.01081059 0.9482546 0.9914852 #> 7.3  7 4.275862 0.9629472 0.9697253 0.02141386 0.8966224 0.9830937 #> 7.4  7 4.413793 0.9447983 0.9546153 0.03178993 0.8453193 0.9748782 #> 7.5  7 4.551724 0.9269025 0.9395565 0.04191772 0.7951691 0.9666450 #> 7.6  7 4.689655 0.9092609 0.9246760 0.05177424 0.7461024 0.9583546 concordance(fit) concordance(fit, time_start = 2, type_weights = "n/G2") auc(fit, time_start = 2, time_horizon = 5) if (!is.null(preds)) {   survival_plot(preds) +     ggtitle(paste("Dynamic Survival Prediction for Subject", target_id)) +     geom_vline(xintercept = dataEvent$time[dataEvent$id == target_id], linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +     annotate("text", x = dataEvent$time[dataEvent$id == target_id], y = 0.1, label = "Observed event time", color = "red", hjust = 1.1) }

title: joinme
text: JoiNMe (package name styled joinme deliberate ambiguity) fits Bayesian joint mixed-effects models multivariate longitudinal markers time--event outcomes. supports multiple outcome families (Gaussian, Student-t, binary, count, beta, ordinal, skewed families), irregular measurement schedule. Current implementation experiments flexible association structures, covariance regression, transform-based modelling nonlinear effects, dynamic prediction. joinme works CmdStanR RStan. package designed recipes : simulate assemble longitudinal event data simulate_joinme(), fit joint model joinme(), inspect posterior draws diagnostics, summarise plot fitted effects, generate dynamic predictions plot future trajectories survival.

title: joinme
text: Trinh Dong, 2026
code: library(joinme)  set.seed(2026)  # Simulate a small dataset sim <- simulate_joinme(   n_id = 10,   families = list(     jm_family("student_t"),     jm_family("student_t", inv_link = ~ inv_logit(x / 2))   ),   n_obs_per_marker_per_id = 4,   times_obs = seq(0, 5, length.out = 8),   quadrature_nodes = 31,   seed = 2026,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   assoc_coefs = c(cv_total = 0.6) )  # Note: when estimating marker weights, compare to sim$truth$marker_weights # because effective marker intensities are used directly from w_raw inside Stan.  formulaLong <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time | id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time | id) | marker)  formulaEvent <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2  fit <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong,   dataLong = sim$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent,   dataEvent = sim$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = list(     jm_family("student_t"),     jm_family("student_t", inv_link = ~ inv_logit(x / 2))   ),   transforms = list(cv_total = list(type = "identity")),   control = list(     parallel_chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 100,     iter_sampling = 100,     seed = 2026,     refresh = 0,     adapt_delta = 0.9   ) )  inherits(fit, "JoiNMeFit")  # Summaries summary(fit) diagnosis(fit) fixef(fit) coef(fit)  # Renamed posterior draws draws(fit, variables = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), format = "draws_df")  # Bayesplot-backed posterior display with renamed variables mcmc_plot(fit, variable = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), type = "trace")  # Conditional effects for either joint-model process profiles <- make_conditions(sim$dataEvent, vars = "x1") ce <- conditional_effects(   fit,   effects = list(longitudinal = "time", event = "x1"),   conditions = profiles,   process = c("longitudinal", "event"),   plot = FALSE ) plot(ce, ask = FALSE)  # Average marker-specific expected responses after applying each inverse link ce_average_marker <- conditional_effects(   fit,   effects = "time",   process = "longitudinal",   longitudinal_estimand = "marginal_marker",   plot = FALSE )  # Random effects / covariance / combined coefficients (nested by formula block) re_fit <- ranef(fit) cf_fit <- coef(fit) vc_fit <- vcov(fit) # Example accessors: # re_fit$formulaLong$id # cf_fit$formulaLong$id # re_fit$formulaDist$sigma$allFamilies # vc_fit$formulaDist$nu$allFamilies  # Dynamic prediction for one subject ndL <- sim$dataLong[sim$dataLong$id == 1, ] ndE <- sim$dataEvent[sim$dataEvent$id == 1, ] time_start <- max(ndL$time)  pred <- posterior_epred(   fit,   newdataLong = ndL,   newdataEvent = ndE,   time_start = time_start,   times = seq(time_start, time_start + 1, length.out = 20),   control = list(n_samples = 50),   seed = 69 )  # Prediction diagnostics + conditional random-effect summaries summary(pred) diagnosis(pred)  # Available only when marker covariance depends on id if (isTRUE(pred$metadata$marker_corr_depends_on_id)) {   re_pred <- ranef(pred)   vc_pred <- vcov(pred) }  # Plot longitudinal and survival predictions plot(pred, type = c("longitudinal", "survival"), combined = TRUE) longitudinal_plot(pred) survival_plot(pred)  # Alternative longitudinal display: posterior mean change heatmap plot(   fit,   type = "longitudinal",   longitudinal_style = "heatmap",   scale = "epred",   threshold = 0.05 )  # Posterior summary/extraction helpers posterior_summary(fit) posterior_fixef(fit) posterior_ranef(fit) posterior_coef(fit) posterior_assoc(fit, summary = TRUE)  # Explicit fitted-object plot helpers association_plot(fit) diagnostic_plot(fit, type = "rhat")  # All coefficient extractors support summary = TRUE/FALSE fixef(fit, summary = TRUE) ranef(fit, summary = FALSE) coef(fit, summary = FALSE)  # For multiple subjects with combined=TRUE: returns one combined plot per subject # (named list). If combiner packages are unavailable, falls back to the # standard subject/outcome nested list. # New marker levels in newdataLong are rejected; prediction marker levels must # match training levels. Dynamic prediction summaries marginalize latent # augmentation noise by averaging across dynpred posterior rows per stored draw.

title: Example: Build Transform Specification from Formula String — example_transform_spec
code: # Example 1: Functional transformation (bytecode-backed) spec_cv <- list(   type = "functional",   expr = ~ (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2 )  # Example 2: Piecewise-linear spec_cs <- list(   type = "pwlin",   knots = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2),   direction = "increasing" )  # Example 3: I-spline (monotonic) # - knots define basis locations (first/last are boundary knots) # - coeff defines the monotone shape directly spec_corr <- list(   type = "ispline",   knots = c(-1, 0, 1),   coeff = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.2, 1.5),   degree = 3 )  # Example 4: Penalised monotone I-spline (fit in R) # - x is the input scale of the raw association feature # - y is the desired transformed output at each x # - lambda controls smoothness (higher = smoother) spec_corr_pen <- list(   type = "ispline_penalised",   x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50),   y = exp(seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50)),   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0,   direction = "increasing" )  # Example 5: Penalised monotone I-spline (Stan-estimated coefficients) # - omit y so Stan learns the monotone shape directly # - if knots are omitted, n_knots = 6 and x quantiles define them spec_corr_pen_stan <- list(   type = "ispline_penalised",   x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50),   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0 )  # Example 6: Penalised monotone I-spline on expit(x) spec_corr_expit <- list(   type = "ispline_expit_penalised",   x = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = 50),   y = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = 50)^0.75,   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0,   direction = "increasing" )  # Combine and build standata transforms <- joinme_tf(   cv_total = spec_cv,   cs_total = spec_cs,   corr = spec_corr ) standata_tf <- joinme:::build_standata_transforms(transforms)

text: formulaLong Longitudinal formula defining fixed effects, id-level effects, marker block. marker block may optionally include inner ( ... | id ) term marker--id random effects. inner term omitted, marker--id random effects disabled (Q_idm = 0). Use || enforce independence. nested marker terms, outer ( ... || marker ) keeps marker-marker--id blocks independent, inner ( ... || id ) makes marker--id covariance diagonal. Grouping terms may use weighted(group, weights = <column>) define formula-scoped positive subject/group weights. dataLong Long-format longitudinal data columns id, marker, time, outcome, covariates referenced formulaLong. formulaEvent Survival formula baseline covariates event model. Supported LHS forms : survival::Surv(time, status) survival::Surv(start, stop, status) survival::Surv(time, status, type = "left") survival::Surv(time1, time2, type = "interval2") legacy type = "interval" form intentionally rejected. dataEvent Event-process data either one row per id (Surv(time, status)) multiple time-split rows per id (Surv(start, stop, status)). Covariates referenced formulaEvent may vary interval split form. formulaVCov Covariance regression formula id-specific marker--id effects. marker block omits inner ( ... | id ), marker--id effects absent covariance-style associations (corr, vcov) allowed. Downstream, corr uses -diagonal entries subject-specific Cholesky-correlation factor K, whereas vcov uses -diagonal K entries together subject-specific standard deviations. corr vcov requested, vcov kept corr ignored warning. default ~ 1 valid yields intercept-covariance regression subject-level slope columns. formulaDist Optional list formulas distributional regression. Supported parameters sigma, nu, phi, alpha, kappa, tau. nu reserved Student-t degrees freedom; kappa positive Beta sample-size parameter defining shapes \(\mu\kappa\) \((1-\mu)\kappa\); tau skew-double-exponential quantile/asymmetry parameter \((0,1)\). Three forms supported: Named list RHS-formulas, e.g. list(sigma = ~ 1 + time). Unnamed list LHS parameter names, e.g. list(sigma ~ 1 + time). Random-effects terms | supported; nested random-effects formulas . Grouping factors distributional random-effects terms may also use weighted(group, weights = <column>). id_var Column name subject id longitudinal event data. marker_var Column name marker/biomarker id longitudinal data. time_var Column name longitudinal time dataLong. eps_fd Positive finite-difference step association derivatives. assoc Character vector specifying association components (e.g., "cv_mean", "cs_total", "corr", "vcov"). corr channel targets -diagonal entries subject-specific Cholesky-correlation factor K; vcov channel targets -diagonal K entries together subject-specific standard deviations. families Optional marker-specific family specification. Can character family names jm_family(...) entries per-marker links. NULL, markers use Gaussian responses identity link. Supported named forward links identity, log, logit, probit, exp; jm_family() also accepts invertible formula link directly specified inverse-link formula. formula syntax, inv_Phi/qnorm/probit denote standard normal quantile Phi/pnorm denote standard normal CDF. Thus probit forward link inverted Phi Stan data constructed. transforms Optional list specifying transformations association terms. element (cv_total, cs_total, corr, vcov) list type fields required type (see build_standata_transforms()). covariance-style terms, transforms apply either -diagonal K features (corr) combined -diagonal K plus subject-specific SD features (vcov). Functional transforms may request fit-affine-shift parameters intercept = TRUE /slope = TRUE inside transform formula. Ordered piecewise-linear fits use list(type = "pwlin", knots = ..., direction = "increasing") ("decreasing"). knot ordinates estimated simplex increments; legacy x accepted alias knots, legacy y longer fixes fitted curve. beta_prior Prior specification longitudinal fixed effects. alpha_prior Prior specification association parameters. iota_prior Prior specification fit-affine-shift intercept slope parameters used functional association transforms. lkj_prior Prior specification correlation structures. allow_marker_crosscorr Integer flag; 1 allows cross-marker correlation marker RE. shrinkage Integer flag controlling shrinkage behaviour marker--id effects. 0 = student_t(6, 0, 1), 1 = double_exponential(0, 1), 2 = std_normal(); marker_weights Optional base weights marker-specific association components. shared_marker_weights = TRUE, provide one numeric vector length D (one named numeric vector keyed marker level) shared across active weighted association terms. shared_marker_weights = FALSE, may instead provide named list entries cv_total, cs_total, cv_marker, cs_marker. supplied entry aligned marker order used matching active weighted association term. fixed_marker_weights Logical; TRUE, marker weights kept fixed marker_weights (perturbation). FALSE, marker weights estimated via signed additive perturbations, marker_weights + z_marker_weights. standardized latent family selected shrinkage: Student-t(6), Laplace, Normal 0, 1, 2. shared_marker_weights Logical; TRUE, active weighted marker-based association terms share one marker-weight structure. FALSE, active weighted marker-based association term gets marker-weight structure. basehaz Baseline hazard basis type: "bs", "ns", "formula". basehaz_n_knots Number internal knots spline baseline hazards. basehaz_knots Optional numeric vector internal knots spline baseline hazards. basehaz_degree Degree spline basis baseline hazard. basehaz_formula Formula baseline hazard basehaz = "formula". tau_spline Prior scale spline coefficients (penalised spline). quadrature_nodes Optional positive integer target total quadrature points. Allowed values exactly 7, 15, 31, 41, 51, 61. node count passed Stan; GK nodes/weights fixed Stan. vcov_diag_link Link subject-specific standard deviation regression: "softplus" "exp". tau_fixed Optional fixed quantile/asymmetry parameter skew double exponential family. must lie strictly zero one; value \(0.5\) gives symmetric double exponential distribution. combined tau distributional regression. seed Optional random seed deterministic components standata. flag_resid_dim Integer flag include residual dimension checks.

title: Functional Transform Builder for Joint Models — parse_transform_expr
text: 0 PUSH_X: Push input x onto stack 1 PUSH_CONST: Push next constant value 2 ADD: Pop b,; push +b 3 SUB: Pop b,; push -b 4 MUL: Pop b,; push *b 5 DIV: Pop b,; push /b 6 LOG: Pop ; push log() 7 EXP: Pop ; push exp() 8 SQRT: Pop ; push sqrt() 9 INV_LOGIT: Pop ; push inv_logit() 10 LOGIT: Pop ; push logit() 11 RECIPROCAL: Pop ; push 1/12 POW: Pop b,; push ^b 13 SIN: Pop ; push sin() 14 COS: Pop ; push cos() 15 TAN: Pop ; push tan() 16 ABS: Pop ; push abs() 17 SQUARE: Pop ; push ^2 18 SINH: Pop ; push sinh() 19 COSH: Pop ; push cosh() 20 TANH: Pop ; push tanh() 21 ASINH: Pop ; push asinh() 22 ACOSH: Pop ; push acosh() 23 ATANH: Pop ; push atanh() 24 SOFTPLUS: Pop ; push log1p_exp() 25 CBRT: Pop ; push cbrt() 26 PHI: Pop ; push standard normal CDF \(\Phi()\) 27 INV_PHI: Pop ; push standard normal quantile \(\Phi^{-1}()\)

title: Functional Transform Builder for Joint Models — parse_transform_expr
code: # Simple: f(x) = x + 2 bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ x + 2)  # Use a plain formula (recommended) bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ log(x + 1)) # Returns: bytecode = c(0, 1, 2), const_data = c(2)  # Complex: f(x) = (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2 bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2)  # The normal CDF and its quantile use separate instructions phi_bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ Phi(x)) probit_bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ inv_Phi(x))

title: Simulate joint model data — simulate_joinme
text: formulaLong Longitudinal formula (role joinme()). Grouping terms may use weighted(group, weights = <column>) mirror fitting syntax. referenced weight column available generated covariates (example via covariate_formulas). nested marker terms, outer ( ... || marker ) keeps marker-marker--id blocks independent, inner ( ... || id ) makes marker--id covariance diagonal. formulaEvent Event/survival formula (role joinme()). formulaVCov Optional covariance-regression formula id-specific marker--id covariance factor (role joinme_standata()). formula evaluated event-level covariates (one row per subject), must include random-effect bars ( ... | ... ), must include longitudinal time variable. Internally, formula drives subject-specific standard deviations Cholesky-correlation-factor rows used build L_i = SD_i * K_i; see re_params$id_marker_cov. default ~ 1 supported gives intercept-covariance regression. formulaDist Optional distributional regression formulas (role joinme()). Supported LHS parameters sigma, nu, phi, alpha (aliases: alpha_skew, skew), kappa, tau. Family-scoped syntax supported square brackets: param[family=<name>] ~ ..., example sigma[family=student_t] ~ 1 + time. bracket used (e.g. sigma ~ 1 + time), formula applies rows parameter exists. bracket used, applies rows family estimated separately scopes. formulaAssoc Optional formula association terms hazard, e.g. ~ cv_total + corr + vcov. provided, overrides assoc. transforms Optional transform specifications association terms. Supports structure joinme(..., transforms=...) cv_total, cv_mean, cv_marker, cs_total, cs_mean, cs_marker, corr, vcov. Simulation applies cv_total cv_marker transforms marker level weighted averaging (aligned fit/predict Stan semantics). Functional transforms support arithmetic common nonlinear functions, including inv_logit/expit/sigmoid, exp, log, sqrt, power, cbrt, softplus/log1p_exp, trigonometric hyperbolic functions, standard normal CDF (Phi, pnorm), standard normal quantile (inv_Phi, qnorm, probit). Quick parameterisation reference: list(type = "identity") omitted term: identity transform (default). list(type = "functional", expr = ~ log1p(x)): functional transform; expr required. list(type = "ispline", knots = c(-1, 0, 1), coeff = c(0, 0.3, 0.8, 1.1, 1.3), degree = 3): direct monotone -spline; degree defaults 3 omitted. list(type = "ispline_penalised", x = seq(-2, 2, length.= 50), y = exp(seq(-2, 2, length.= 50)), n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1): penalised monotone -spline; defaults n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1 omitted. list(type = "ispline_expit", knots = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), coeff = c(0, 0.25, 0.8, 1.0, 1.1), degree = 3): monotone -spline evaluated plogis(x); explicit knots supplied expit scale. list(type = "ispline_expit_penalised", x = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.= 50), y = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.= 50)^0.8, n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1): penalised monotone -spline plogis(x) legacy plug-mode. list(type = "pwlin", x = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), y = c(0.2, 0.5, 1, 0.5, 0.2)): piecewise-linear transform; x y required. Simulation deliberately treats fixed interpolation pairs. differs model fitting, knot ordinates estimated ordered simplex construction y longer fixes curve. monotone spline transforms simulation: type = "ispline": provide knots coeff directly (plus optional degree). type = "ispline_penalised" (alias: "ispline_penalized"): provide training pairs x y, plus smoothness penalty lambda. simulator fits monotone spline R evaluating transformed association. fitted plug-spline uses anchored endpoint coefficients matching Stan-estimated path: increasing splines run 0 1, decreasing splines run 1 0. direction omitted, simulator infers supplied (x, y) pairs. type = "ispline_expit" / "ispline_expit_penalised": semantics ordinary -spline variants , except spline basis built plogis(x) bounded-domain representation. Training x values explicit knots transform types specified bounded expit scale. useful raw association feature long tails steep nonlinear effects. words, simulation currently uses legacy plug-spline mode; estimate spline coefficients jointly inside Stan. n_id Number subjects. families Marker-specific family names. Use jm_family() entries supply custom link/inv_link expressions. named probit link applies Phi inverse link. formula expressions, Phi/pnorm standard normal CDF inv_Phi/qnorm/probit standard normal quantile. Simulation evaluates bytecode instructions fitting prediction. marker_levels Optional marker names; defaults m1, m2, ... times_obs Scheduled observation time grid used every (id, marker) optional visit-time jitter post-event censoring applied. obs_time_noise_sd Optional Gaussian noise SD added independently simulated observation time visit schedule chosen; noisy visit times clipped [0, time_cens]. censor_longitudinal_after_event Logical; TRUE (default), simulated longitudinal observations truncated subject event time. FALSE, longitudinal schedule may continue event time time_cens. left_truncation_max Optional non-negative delayed-entry bound. > 0, subject receives sampled entry [0, min(left_truncation_max, stop_time)). truncate_longitudinal_before_entry Logical; TRUE delayed entry active (left_truncation_max > 0), longitudinal rows observed sampled entry time removed. ... Additional arguments passed fun. seed RNG seed. covariate_formulas Named LHS formulas used generate event-level covariates, e.g. list(x1 ~ rnorm(n_id), x2 ~ rt(n_id, df = 5)). Time-varying step covariates supported via time_varyring(fun, n_step, steps, ...), example list(x ~ time_varyring(rnorm, c(3, 6), mean = 0, sd = 1)) list(x ~ time_varyring(rnorm, steps = c(1, 3, 5), mean = 0, sd = 1)). mode, id receives stepwise periods [0, time_cens], period value sampled fun. marker_weights Optional base marker weights used association aggregation. shared_marker_weights = TRUE, supply one numeric vector shared across active weighted marker-based association terms. shared_marker_weights = FALSE, may instead supply named list entries cv_total, cs_total, cv_marker, cs_marker. shared_marker_weights Logical. TRUE, active weighted marker-based association terms share one marker-weight structure. FALSE, active weighted marker-based association term uses marker-weight structure. fixed_marker_weights Logical. meaning joinme(). TRUE, marker_weights effective weights latent perturbation drawn. FALSE (default), marker_weights base weights effective weights marker_weights + z_marker_weights. base weights omitted default zero, exactly joinme() marker weights estimated. shrinkage Integer selecting distribution standardized latent marker-weight perturbation fixed_marker_weights = FALSE: 0 draws Student-t 6 degrees freedom, 1 draws standard Laplace, 2 draws standard Normal. switch used Stan priors. change explicitly supplied fixed weights. assoc Association components (names fit): cv_total, cv_mean, cv_marker, cs_total, cs_mean, cs_marker, corr, vcov. Meaning channel: cv_*: current-value channels longitudinal trajectories, cs_*: current-slope channels finite differences (eps_cs), corr: -diagonal entries subject-specific Cholesky-correlation factor K marker--id random effects. vcov: -diagonal K entries together subject-specific standard deviations. can also provide formulaAssoc = ~ ... select channels; present, overrides assoc. assoc_coefs Association coefficients hazard terms. Non-corr/vcov terms accept scalar values. corr term accepts vector -diagonal K coefficients ordered (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), ... lower-triangular row-major order marker--id random-effect covariance dimension. vcov term accepts -diagonal K entries followed subject-specific standard deviations, (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), ..., sd_1, sd_2, ...; || used marker--id random-effects block, standard deviation entries used. Accepted input forms: named numeric vector, e.g. c(cv_total = 0.4, cs_mean = -0.2), named list, e.g. list(cv_total = 0.4, corr = c(0.2, -0.1), vcov = c(0.4, 0.1, 0.5)). Missing channels default 0. beta_long Fixed-effect coefficients formulaLong fixed part. NULL, coefficients randomly generated named model-matrix columns. beta_event Survival baseline-covariate coefficients non-intercept terms formulaEvent RHS. NULL, coefficients randomly generated. dist_coefs Distributional fixed-effect coefficients formulaDist parameters (sigma, nu, phi, alpha, kappa, tau). parameter, coefficients can : unnamed numeric vector (matched column order), named numeric vector (matched model-matrix column names), family-scoped formulas, named list per-scope entries. Family-scoped list syntax examples: dist_coefs = list(sigma = list(default = c("(Intercept)" = -0.3), gaussian = c(...), student_t = c(...))) alias keys like "sigma[family='student_t']" also recognised mapped matching family scope. re_params Random-effects simulation controls. Structure: id: controls id-level random effects ( ... | id) formulaLong. marker: controls marker-level random effects marker-terms. id_marker_cov: controls subject-specific covariance-regression marker--id latent effects. dist: controls random effects distributional regressions formulaDist. id marker, block list: sd: scalar length-K vector random-effect standard deviations, corr: KxK correlation matrix. id_marker_cov fields: latent: deprecated compatibility input. supplied, implied lower-triangular factor folded baseline alpha intercepts simulation. Marker--id latent seeds still drawn iid standard normal values. Prefer setting alpha directly new code. alpha: baseline linear predictors subject-specific covariance regression entries. Diagonal positions control standard deviations; -diagonal positions control row-wise correlation-factor regression, tanh scale. beta: covariate effects formulaVCov design matrix (systematic subject--subject covariance shifts observed covariates), lambda: non-negative loading iid standard-normal subject latent perturbation; negative value supplied, simulator folds sign latent draw effective model remains unchanged follows identified convention used fitting, diag_link: link subject-specific standard deviations ("softplus" "exp"). Element-wise covariance-regression form : eta_{im} = alpha_m + x_i^T beta_m + lambda_m z_{im}, lambda_m >= 0 z_{im} ~ Normal(0, 1). Diagonal entries apply diag_link give positive subject-specific standard deviations. -diagonal entries mapped tanh assembled row row valid subject-specific Cholesky-correlation factor K_i. covariance factor reconstructed L_i = SD_i * K_i. Marker--id latent seeds sampled iid standard normal values final marker--id effects obtained b_id = L_i z_id. Dimension rules id_marker_cov entries follow marker--id random-effect dimension Q_idm: covariance full: M = Q_idm * (Q_idm + 1) / 2 lower-tri entries, covariance forced diagonal (|| nested id-marker term): M = Q_idm. dist block syntax: re_params$dist[[param]] applies random-effect terms distributional parameter, re_params$dist[[param]]$terms[[j]] optionally sets term-specific controls (sd/corr fields ). family_params Family-specific constants used corresponding parameter distributional regression. particular, specify Beta mean/sample-size model beta = list(kappa = ...) skew double exponential model skew_double_exponential = list(sigma = ..., tau = ...). kappa must positive. tau must lie \((0,1)\), \(0.5\) giving symmetric double exponential distribution. h0 Optional baseline hazard function h0(t) supplied, takes precedence baseline_hazard/formulaBasehaz. baseline_hazard Optional baseline hazard specification. Supported forms: character: one "constant", "linear", "piecewise", "weibull", "spline". named list: list(type = ..., ...) mode-specific parameters. formulaBasehaz Optional formula-based baseline hazard model time, e.g. ~ 1 + time + (time^2). beta_basehaz Optional coefficients formulaBasehaz (aligned model-matrix column names). NULL, coefficients generated. time_cens Administrative censoring horizon. eps_cs Finite-difference step slope-type associations (cs_*). integration_control Control list passed integrate(). root_control Root finding control inverse-CDF sampling. quadrature_nodes Optional Gauss-Kronrod node count simulation-side survival integration. Allowed values: 7, 15, 31, 41, 51, 61. n_workers Number workers use use_mirai = TRUE. use_mirai Logical; TRUE n_workers > 1, use mirai parallel simulation available. Parallel jobs seeded deterministically main seed reproducible simulations. id_var, marker_var, time_var, y_var, event_time_var, event_var Column names aligned joinme_standata() defaults. fun Function apply. x Numeric vector link scale. inv_link_bc Parsed inverse-link bytecode.
